chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who said, 'For the sake of Allah, upon me is the walking to the Kaaba if I buy something on credit for my family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is that difficult for them?' He said: 'Yes, it is difficult for them if he does not take something for them on credit.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him take it for them on credit, and there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.الْمَشْيُ إِلَى الْكَعْبَةِ: Walking to the Kaaba (a form of vow or pilgrimage)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty or fulfillment required)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional vow to walk to the Kaaba if one buys goods on credit?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the vow's condition is fulfilled by the act of purchasing on credit, as the core intent was to provide for the family rather than the specific method of payment. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of interpreting vows according to their practical purpose (maqasid) rather than rigid literalism, ensuring ease for the vow-maker. It underscores the flexibility in fulfilling conditional vows when the underlying benefit is achieved.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about a man who said, ‘For the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, upon me is the walking to the Kaaba if I can buy something on credit for my family’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is that suffering upon them?’ He said, ‘Yes, that is suffering upon them if he cannot take something for them on credit’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him take it for them on credit, and there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says, ‘It is on me to walk to al-Ka’bah if I can buy certain things for my family on credit. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is that difficult on them?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it is difficult for them not to take for them anything on credit.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must take for them on credit and he does not owe anything.’”
